findings.location: gso::opt1-102 fields version and version_status (c2; also c1 version check)
findings.evidence: Row claims version_status "published" with version "opt1-102", which per c2 means the maintainer publishes a release identifier for this board and version copies it. Neither the protocol page (Source 1) nor the complete leaderboard.json (Source 2) contains any release identifier: the string "opt1-102" appears nowhere, and leaderboard metadata offers only last_updated "2026-09-27" and total_tasks 102. c2 states a page that publishes no release identifier supports "snapshot"; thus "published" is a mismatch, and "opt1-102" matches neither allowed state (not a maintainer identifier, not snapshot-<date>).
findings.repair: Set version_status to "snapshot" and version to "snapshot-2026-11-09" (this run's capture date) per the registry freeze convention, or supply maintainer evidence of a published release identifier if one actually exists.

findings.evidence: Notes cite the page changelog for the 2026-04-27 iteration-budget increase and the 2026-07-12 network isolation, but omit the changelog's 2026-09-27 entry ("Improved elicitation to explicitly ask models to keep measuring and improving after their first speedup") present in Source 1; the four newest leaderboard rows are dated 2026-09-27 and were produced under that elicitation change, so the stated configuration history is incomplete relative to the changelog it invokes.
findings.repair: Add the 2026-09-27 elicitation change to scoring.notes so the noted configuration history matches the changelog, or state explicitly that notes list only selected changes.

uncertainties: I cannot recompute SHA-256 hashes or execute transport and qualification checks; owner-computed row, source and artifact hashes are accepted as binding per the packet, and this limitation is not treated as missing evidence.

Source 1 is a bounded excerpt of the protocol page; the f1 'published' mismatch rests on the supplied excerpt plus the complete leaderboard.json capture never showing any release identifier, and I cannot fetch the live page to re-confirm.

The maintainer string 'GSO team (UC Berkeley)' includes a Berkeley affiliation that the supplied protocol excerpt never states explicitly (it shows the GSO name and the author list only); maintainer is outside the c1/c2 check list, so this is noted rather than failed.

Unit 'percent' and range [0,100] were judged only against Source 4's generated scale summary (32 finite values, lowest 0, highest 88.24) as c1 permits; that summary was not used to infer metric meaning.

status "active" is supported by Source 3's generated activity summary (4 new values on 2026-09-27 rows) and by metadata.last_updated 2026-09-27; superseded_by null is uncontradicted because the protocol names no successor board.
